title: I Ran My First Ultramarathon (50K Trail Race)
creator: Kofi Runs
description:
50 kilometers, 1,300 meters of climbing, one very bad descent. Here's how my first ultra went and what I'd do differently.

Race: Ridgeback 50K
Shoes: the same pair as my last three videos
Strava: kofiruns

1:10 The fueling mistake
2:40 The good part

4:00 Lessons

sentences.t: So I did it, I ran fifty kilometers on Saturday, and I am currently walking down stairs backwards.
This was my first ultra, a trail race up in the hills, with about thirteen hundred meters of climbing.
I want to walk you through how it went, what I got wrong, and what I'd change.
The start was at six a.m., still dark, everyone with headlamps on.
My plan was simple, go out slow, slower than feels right, and hike every hill steeper than a driveway.
And for the first ten K, I actually did that.
Which, for me, is a miracle.
Around kilometer twelve, there's this long climb up a fire road, and I got sucked into chatting with a guy from Denver.
We were talking about everything, and I totally forgot to eat.
That was mistake number one.
By the top of that climb, I could feel that first little wave of, hm, this is not great.
So I took a gel, slowed down, and things came back around kilometer eighteen.
Hydration was the thing I worried about most going into this.
In training I cramped on every long run over three hours, and my calves would just lock up.
And what fixed that for me was getting my sodium sorted.
I've been using Saltline for about four months now.
It's an electrolyte mix with way more sodium than the usual sports drinks, about a thousand milligrams a serving, and almost no sugar.
It comes in these little stick packs, so I keep two in my vest and dump one into a soft flask at every aid station.
The citrus one tastes like lemonade that went to the gym, which I mean as a compliment.
Since I switched, I haven't had a single cramp, including all fifty K on Saturday.
If you want to try it, use code KOFI for twenty percent off your first order at saltline.co slash kofi.
There's also a sampler pack with all six flavors if you're not sure which one you'll like.
Okay, back to the race.
The aid station at kilometer twenty-five had boiled potatoes dipped in salt, and I think I ate six.
Kilometers twenty-five to thirty-five were honestly the best part of the day.
The trail goes along a ridge, the sun was coming through the trees, and I felt unstoppable.
Then kilometer thirty-eight happened.
There's a descent that just goes straight down for about three kilometers, rocky and loose, and my quads gave out completely.
I was walking downhill, people were passing me, and I had a real conversation with myself about dropping out.
What got me through was breaking it into tiny pieces, just get to the next ribbon, then the next one.
The last five K were flat, and I shuffled them at a pace I'm not going to say out loud.
But I crossed the line in seven hours and forty-two minutes.
My goal was under eight, so I'll take it.
So, lessons.
One, eat on a timer, every thirty minutes, whether you feel like it or not.
Two, train downhills, not just uphills, because the downhills are what wrecked me.
Three, have a mantra or a trick for the low points, because there will be low points.
Would I do another one?
Ask me in two weeks.
Okay, probably yes.
If you're training for your first ultra, tell me which race in the comments, and I'll see you in the next one.
